data.source_text_main_point: Aaron Swartz, an open source programmer and Harvard fellow, faces federal fraud charges for downloading millions of academic papers from JSTOR, an act that has sparked a public debate over copyright enforcement and access to knowledge.

statements.key_statement: Aaron Swartz faces federal fraud charges for downloading millions of academic papers from JSTOR.
statements.long_statement: Aaron Swartz, a Harvard fellow and open source programmer, was arrested and charged with multiple federal fraud counts after downloading two-thirds of JSTOR's academic journal repository by connecting a laptop to the MIT network. This legal action stems from the broader debate regarding the enforcement of copyright laws versus public access to scholarly information.

statements.key_statement: Aaron Swartz entered a not guilty plea and was freed on an unsecured bond worth $100,000.
statements.long_statement: Aaron Swartz was released on a $100,000 unsecured bond after pleading not guilty to all federal fraud charges, a legal status that allows him to remain free while awaiting trial for the alleged unauthorized downloading of millions of academic papers from JSTOR.
